**Answer: 1000**

**Setup.** Split the 19 rows and 19 columns into groups {1,2}, {3,4}, …, {17,18}, {19}. This gives 10 groups each, so 100 blocks. Any two cells in one block are king-adjacent, so each block holds at most one selected cell. Selecting 99 cells therefore means exactly one block is empty and every other block holds exactly one cell.

**Offsets.** Write each selected cell's row as 2i−1+a and column as 2j−1+b, with offsets a, b ∈ {0,1}. Group 10 has only offset 0. Two cells in neighboring blocks conflict only in these patterns:
- vertically adjacent blocks: upper a=1 and lower a=0;
- horizontally adjacent blocks: left b=1 and right b=0;
- diagonal blocks: the cell pattern (a,b) must match the corresponding conjunction.

**Forced structure.**
- A band (row-group) with no empty block has a complete horizontal chain. The chain must be nondecreasing in b and ends at b=0 (group 10), so all its b are 0. Similarly, a column-group with no empty block has all a=0.
- Let the empty block be (p,q). Then every block outside row p and column q has a=b=0. The remaining free offsets are:
  - b(p,1) ≤ … ≤ b(p,q−1), a nondecreasing binary sequence of length L=q−1, giving L+1 choices;
  - a(1,q) ≤ … ≤ a(p−1,q), a nondecreasing binary sequence of length M=p−1, giving M+1 choices.
- The only extra diagonal conflict is between blocks (p−1,q) and (p,q−1), which forbids a(p−1,q)=1 together with b(p,q−1)=1. Both sequences end in 1 in ML of the (M+1)(L+1) combinations, so the number of valid choices is (M+1)(L+1) − ML = M+L+1 = p+q−1.

**Total.**
$$\sum_{p=1}^{10}\sum_{q=1}^{10}(p+q-1)=\sum_{p,q}(p+q)-100=1100-100=1000.$$

**Check.** The same method on a 3×3 grid gives Σ_{p,q∈{1,2}}(p+q−1) = 8. Direct enumeration of the 3-cell independent sets of the 3×3 king graph also gives 8.

ANSWER: 1000
